families.name: Dependence & Withdrawal Physiology
families.definition: Physiological adaptation and withdrawal severity following reduction or cessation of repeated substance exposure.
families.includes: Nicotine, caffeine, alcohol, cannabis, and opioid withdrawal severity.
families.exclusions: Addiction identity, access, stigma, or treatment systems.

families.name: Endocrine & Reproductive Physiology
families.definition: Endocrine and reproductive physiological variables that alter bodily regulation and functional capacity.
families.includes: Thyroid status, maturation, pregnancy-related load, menopausal transition, reproductive hormonal state, and physiological arousal.
families.exclusions: Sex/gender categories or simplistic single-hormone explanations of complex behavior.

families.name: Fatigue, Pain & Physical Capacity
families.definition: Bodily capacity and burden variables that alter effort, attention, movement, and protective responding.
families.includes: Physical and cognitive fatigue, acute and persistent pain, and physical functional capacity.
families.exclusions: Workload or task demands themselves; diagnoses without a specified functional state.

families.name: Homeostatic & Interoceptive Regulation
families.definition: Internal physiological need and visceral states that signal departures from bodily equilibrium.
families.includes: Hunger, satiety, thirst, hydration, glucose availability, nausea, breathlessness, and visceral urgency.
families.exclusions: Food access, ambient conditions, preferences, and beliefs about bodily states.

families.name: Immune & Inflammatory Physiology
families.definition: Immune signaling and coordinated sickness responses that reallocate energy and alter activity and social motivation.
families.includes: Systemic inflammatory activity and sickness-response intensity.
families.exclusions: A named infection alone, psychiatric symptoms, or inflammation used as a catch-all explanation.

families.name: Neurodevelopment, Aging & Reserve
families.definition: Developmental maturation, aging burden, and reserve variables that alter behavioral capacities and susceptibility.
families.includes: Neurodevelopmental maturity, biological aging burden, and frailty severity.
families.exclusions: Chronological age alone or cohort effects.

families.name: Neurological Integrity & Brain State
families.definition: Functional consequences of acute or chronic disruption to brain integrity and arousal.
families.includes: TBI burden, acute encephalopathy, postictal impairment, focal neurological impairment, and neurodegenerative impairment.
families.exclusions: A diagnosis without specified functional burden; normal cognitive differences; imaging activation as a driver.

families.name: Nutritional, Metabolic & Hematologic Status
families.definition: Longer-duration biological variables governing energy sufficiency, oxygen transport, micronutrient status, and glucose regulation.
families.includes: Nutritional energy sufficiency, oxygen-carrying capacity, iron/B12 status, and glycemic regulation.
families.exclusions: Short-term hunger; BMI; broad metabolic-disease labels without a specified variable.

families.name: Oxygenation & Thermoregulatory Physiology
families.definition: Internal oxygenation, carbon-dioxide, and thermal-strain variables affecting neural and physical function.
families.includes: Tissue oxygen availability, intermittent hypoxemia, carbon-dioxide burden, heat strain, and cold strain.
families.exclusions: Altitude, ventilation, weather, or temperature as external exposures.

families.name: Psychoactive & Pharmacologic Effects
families.definition: Current dose-related physiological and neurobehavioral effects of substances and medications.
families.includes: Alcohol, THC, nicotine, caffeine, sedative, opioid, stimulant, and aggregate medication burdens.
families.exclusions: Substance availability, social meaning, identity, or legal status.

families.name: Sensory & Vestibular Capacity
families.definition: Biological capacities and internal sensory burdens governing access to auditory, visual, olfactory, balance, and bodily-position information.
families.includes: Auditory, visual, olfactory, vestibular, somatosensory/proprioceptive capacity, and tinnitus burden.
families.exclusions: External information quality or device/interface accessibility.

families.name: Sleep & Circadian Regulation
families.definition: Variables governing sleep amount, continuity, circadian timing, and sleep–wake transitions.
families.includes: Sleep quantity or continuity, endogenous phase, alignment, chronotype fit, and awakening impairment.
families.exclusions: External schedules and light conditions themselves; subjective fatigue when modeled separately.

families.name: Stable Biological Susceptibility
families.definition: Relatively stable inherited biological profiles that modify susceptibility without determining behavior.
families.includes: Trait- or outcome-specific polygenic liability profiles when appropriately validated.
families.exclusions: Race/ancestry essentialism, single-gene explanations, heritability as destiny, or gene–environment interaction treated as a node.

families.name: Stress, Autonomic & Allostatic Physiology
families.definition: Physiological activation, regulation, recovery, and cumulative burden of stress-response systems.
families.includes: HPA/SAM activation, autonomic arousal, recovery, reactivity, and multisystem allostatic burden.
families.exclusions: Psychological appraisal, external threat, or broad psychiatric diagnoses.

families.name: Affect & Emotion
families.definition: Subjective affective states whose intensity, valence, or activation can alter appraisal, attention, choice, and action readiness.
families.includes: Discrete emotions, mood valence, subjective arousal, stress, frustration, empathy-related affect, and enjoyment.
families.exclusions: Physiological arousal as a biological variable, emotion-regulation processes, and stable affective traits.

families.name: Agency, Attribution & Moral Judgment
families.definition: Appraisals of agency, responsibility, intention, freedom, accountability, and moral obligation that shape blame, sanction, resistance, and principled action.
families.includes: Agency, causal and responsibility attribution, intentionality, freedom threat, reactance, moral conviction, and moral obligation.
families.exclusions: Formal accountability systems, social sanctions themselves, or identity centrality.

families.name: Attention & Cognitive Processing
families.definition: State variables governing allocation of attention, available processing capacity, representational framing, elaboration, and processing ease or flexibility.
families.includes: Attention allocation, salience, cognitive load, working-memory availability, elaboration, construal, fluency, and cognitive flexibility.
families.exclusions: Stored knowledge or memory representations (F07), executive self-regulation (F09), and stable need for cognition (F14).

families.name: Beliefs, Attitudes & Outcome Expectancies
families.definition: Evaluative and propositional variables representing what a person believes about an action, its consequences, and its personal relevance.
families.includes: Behavior-specific evaluations, belief confidence, expected consequences, expected success, relevance, and outcome value.
families.exclusions: Threat/coping appraisals (F02), source judgments (F13), knowledge structures (F07), and goals or intentions (F04).

families.name: Decision Valuation Across Risk, Time & Effort
families.definition: Parameters and state-dependent valuations that shape choice under gains, losses, delay, effort, risk, ambiguity, and default structures.
families.includes: Loss sensitivity, reference points, probability weighting, risk/ambiguity preference, temporal and effort discounting, present bias, decision conflict, and default preference.
families.exclusions: Objective payoffs, choice architecture outside the person, or broad attitudes toward a behavior.

families.name: Epistemic Trust & Persuasion
families.definition: Judgments and motivational states governing acceptance, rejection, search, confidence, and resistance when evaluating information and sources.
families.includes: Source credibility, perceived argument strength, counterarguing, metacognitive confidence, resistance motivation, epistemic trust, and perceived information sufficiency.
families.exclusions: Objective source properties, information quality, channel affordances, and general cognitive capacity.

families.name: Knowledge, Memory & Mental Representation
families.definition: Variables describing accessible knowledge, remembered familiarity and confidence, causal beliefs, and the coherence of internal situation models.
families.includes: Causal-belief strength, mental-model coherence, domain knowledge, memory accessibility, familiarity, memory confidence, and prior-belief congruence.
families.exclusions: Information properties outside the person, processing operations, and reinforcement contingencies.

families.name: Learning, Habit & Automaticity
families.definition: Learned action propensities and associations that permit cues and expected reinforcement to guide behavior with reduced deliberation.
families.includes: Habit strength, automaticity, cue-response associations, reinforcement expectations, and socially learned expectancies.
families.exclusions: The learning mechanism itself, raw repetition counts, or deliberate implementation plans.

families.name: Motivation, Goals & Psychological Needs
families.definition: Variables that energize, direct, prioritize, and sustain intended action, including goal properties and experienced need satisfaction.
families.includes: Intentions, goal attributes, motivational regulation, approach/avoidance orientation, need satisfaction, and anticipated regret.
families.exclusions: Action plans and monitoring processes (F09), trait dispositions (F14), or outcome expectancies (F01).

families.name: Normative & Relational Perceptions
families.definition: Internal perceptions of what others do or approve, and of the quality, fairness, legitimacy, support, and standing experienced in relationships or groups.
families.includes: Perceived norms, approval, support, belonging, trust, fairness, legitimacy, exclusion, and status.
families.exclusions: Actual network structure, observed group behavior, institutional rules, or cultural norms as external conditions.

families.name: Planning, Self-Regulation & Executive Control
families.definition: Variables enabling prospective planning, monitoring, inhibition, attentional control, emotion management, and correction of goal-directed action.
families.includes: Implementation intentions, plan specificity, monitoring, goal discrepancy, regulatory capacity, inhibitory control, and coping flexibility.
families.exclusions: Goal content or motivation (F04), momentary cognitive load (F06), and stable trait self-control (F14).

families.name: Risk, Threat & Coping Appraisal
families.definition: Subjective appraisals of likelihood, severity, control, efficacy, capability, and helplessness in relation to threats or difficult demands.
families.includes: Perceived vulnerability, severity, controllability, response efficacy, personal capability, and coping capacity.
families.exclusions: Objective hazards, physiological stress responses, general affect, and stable punishment sensitivity.

families.name: Self-Concept, Identity & Consistency
families.definition: Variables describing the salience, centrality, clarity, fusion, and threatened or inconsistent state of personal and social self-representations.
families.includes: Behavioral self-identity, identity salience/centrality, social identification, fusion, self-concept clarity, integrity or identity threat, and dissonance.
families.exclusions: Demographic labels, group membership itself, cultural identity content, and moral judgments about particular acts.

families.name: Stable Dispositions & Temperament
families.definition: Relatively enduring individual-difference parameters that systematically bias appraisal, motivation, affect, and self-regulation across situations.
families.includes: Broad personality traits, impulsivity, sensation seeking, reward/punishment sensitivity, need for cognition, need for closure, and intolerance of uncertainty.
families.exclusions: Demographic labels, diagnoses, transient states, or claims that traits determine behavior regardless of context.

families.name: Audience & Social Evaluation
families.definition: Observable social-evaluation conditions created when other people can witness, identify, monitor, or evaluate an actor and an action.
families.includes: Audience presence and size, actor identifiability, action publicness, evaluation exposure, and peer monitoring intensity.
families.exclusions: Evaluation apprehension or reputational concern (Psychological), sensor surveillance (Technological), and formal audit regimes (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Cooperation, Reciprocity & Mutual Dependence
families.definition: Relational conditions governing reliable exchange, mutual aid, repeated cooperation, resource sharing, and vulnerability to free riding.
families.includes: Partner reliability, cooperation prevalence, reciprocity balance, repeated interaction, mutual aid, resource sharing, and free-riding prevalence.
families.exclusions: Interpersonal trust or fairness appraisals, prosocial traits, formal contracts, and cooperation as an unanalyzed behavioral outcome.

families.name: Coordination, Accountability & Collective Capacity
families.definition: Group-level conditions that make coordinated action feasible by aligning goals, expectations, knowledge, roles, responsibility, and answerability.
families.includes: Task interdependence, goal alignment, common knowledge, expectation alignment, collective efficacy, role clarity, identifiable contributions, responsibility concentration, and peer accountability.
families.exclusions: Individual self-efficacy or intentions, formal compliance systems, communication-channel properties, and collective action outcomes.

families.name: Direct Social Influence Conditions
families.definition: Observable properties of other people and influence settings that change the social evidence, pressure, or models available to an actor.
families.includes: Majority size and unanimity, minority consistency, peer presence and exposure, and socially relevant model similarity or status.
families.exclusions: Conformity itself, internal normative or informational influence mechanisms, persuasion judgments, and message-content properties.

families.name: Group Composition, Cohesion & Deliberation
families.definition: Properties of bounded groups that shape participation, information pooling, dissent, subgroup formation, and sustained joint activity.
families.includes: Group size, cohesion, turnover, roles, opinion diversity, dissent availability, participation equality, shared-information coverage, and factionalization.
families.exclusions: Individual identity or emotion, performance outcomes, formal governance rules, and group labels without a varying property.

families.name: Inclusion, Support & Social Integration
families.definition: Observable access to relationships, supportive transactions, participation, and exclusion that embed or isolate an actor within a social system.
families.includes: Personal-network size and breadth, support availability and receipt, inclusion and ostracism events, and objective social isolation.
families.exclusions: Perceived support, loneliness, belonging, attachment needs, and clinical or health outcomes.

families.name: Interaction & Relational Embeddedness
families.definition: Properties of recurring interpersonal interaction and dyadic ties that determine access, obligation, familiarity, and relational constraint.
families.includes: Interaction amount, relationship duration and stability, closeness, reciprocity, multiplexity, and negative interaction frequency.
families.exclusions: Perceived belonging or trust, network-wide topology, formal role assignments, and one-off behavior without a relational state.

families.name: Intergroup Contact, Boundaries & Competition
families.definition: Relational conditions connecting or separating social groups and governing contact, friendship, cooperation, competition, interdependence, and relative position between them.
families.includes: Intergroup contact and friendship, cross-group ties, competition and cooperation, resource interdependence, boundary permeability, inequality, and cross-cutting memberships.
families.exclusions: Threat, prejudice, anxiety, identification, or outgroup evaluation (Psychological), cultural meanings, and formal segregation policies.

families.name: Network Exposure & Social Diffusion
families.definition: Relational exposure conditions through which behaviors, practices, and social signals reach an actor through a network.
families.includes: Proportion, frequency, independence, reinforcement, referent influence, and cross-cluster composition of network exposure.
families.exclusions: Information accuracy or framing, algorithmic ranking, adoption behavior itself, and influence inferred from observational similarity alone.

families.name: Network Structure & Position
families.definition: Graph-level and actor-position variables describing connectivity, closure, brokerage, assortative mixing, and separation in social networks.
families.includes: Recognized network measures with explicit relational meaning, including centrality, density, clustering, constraint, cross-cluster ties, and segregation.
families.exclusions: Platform algorithms, raw trace counts without a defined network, perceived network position, and diffusion outcomes.

families.name: Normative Climate & Informal Enforcement
families.definition: Group-level behavioral regularities, expressed approval patterns, and informal reinforcement conditions that make conduct more or less socially expected.
families.includes: Observed behavioral prevalence, publicly expressed approval, consensus, trends, visibility, and informal social rewards or sanctions.
families.exclusions: An individual's perceived norms (Psychological), deeply shared cultural meanings (Cultural), and formal rules or penalties (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Status, Reputation & Relational Power
families.definition: Socially conferred rank, standing, deference, and asymmetric control that structure whose preferences and actions carry weight.
families.includes: Status rank and hierarchy shape, reputation, deference, resource or dependence asymmetry, and informal authority.
families.exclusions: Status motives or perceived status (Psychological), demographic labels, and authority defined solely by law or office (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Collective Memory, Narrative & Symbolic Meaning
families.definition: Durable shared representations of history, group continuity, causal stories, symbols, and interpretive schemas.
families.includes: Culture-level salience, centrality, consensus, and persistence of memories, narratives, myths, schemas, and symbolic boundaries.
families.exclusions: Individual memory accessibility or belief (Psychological) and properties of a specific message or artifact (Informational).

families.name: Cultural Identity, Boundaries & Change
families.definition: Shared cultural representations that define collective continuity, prototypes, boundaries, accommodation, and receptivity to change.
families.includes: Culture-level identity narratives, prototype consensus, boundary rigidity, assimilation expectations, continuity norms, and generational cultural distance.
families.exclusions: Individual identity salience or acculturation orientation (Psychological), group membership (Social), and citizenship status (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Cultural Transmission & Social Learning
families.definition: Culture-level rates and patterned pathways through which variants are copied, retained, and transmitted across people and generations.
families.includes: Observable transmission prevalence, fidelity, and weighting toward majority, prestige, success, parent, or elder models.
families.exclusions: Learning as an unmeasured mechanism, individual observational expectancies (Psychological), and platform recommendation properties (Technological).

families.name: Emotion Culture & Display Rules
families.definition: Culturally transmitted expectations about desirable emotions and the appropriate expression, restraint, or regulation of affect.
families.includes: Shared ideal-affect priorities and domain-specific display, restraint, anger, and shame norms.
families.exclusions: Experienced emotion intensity and regulation capacity, which remain Psychological.

families.name: Epistemic, Cognitive & Temporal Conventions
families.definition: Shared interpretive conventions about attention, explanation, knowledge legitimacy, contradiction, time, and fate.
families.includes: Culture-level prevalence of reasoning, attribution, epistemic-authority, temporal, and fatalistic conventions.
families.exclusions: Individual attention, attribution, cognitive style, risk preference, or belief strength (Psychological).

families.name: Honor, Face, Dignity & Hierarchy Logics
families.definition: Shared systems defining how social worth is established, threatened, defended, and recognized.
families.includes: Culture-level honor, face, dignity, prestige, deference, and reputation-defense expectations.
families.exclusions: Personal status motives or threat appraisals (Psychological), actual rank and reputation (Social), and formal authority (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Kinship, Family & Communal Obligation
families.definition: Culturally transmitted expectations governing duties to kin, family roles, lineage, guests, and the wider community.
families.includes: Shared obligation strength, role prescriptiveness, loyalty, hospitality, and communal resource-sharing expectations.
families.exclusions: Demographic family labels, actual network ties (Social), private attachment or belonging (Psychological), and family law (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Language & Communication Conventions
families.definition: Culturally shared pragmatic rules governing directness, politeness, status marking, explicitness, silence, and euphemism.
families.includes: Stable communication conventions that can be assessed across interactions, corpora, and community judgments.
families.exclusions: Language identity labels, properties of a specific message (Informational), and transmission-channel features (Technological).

families.name: Norm Strength & Informal Rules
families.definition: Durable, widely transmitted properties of informal rules that govern the strength, scope, persistence, and acceptability of deviation.
families.includes: Culture-level norm entrenchment, tightness, scope, deviance tolerance, and domain-specific informal rules.
families.exclusions: Immediate-group prevalence and sanctions (Social), perceived norms (Psychological), and codified rules or penalties (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Ritual, Tradition & Cultural Practice
families.definition: Culturally shared expectations and properties that give recurring rituals, traditions, and practices behavioral force.
families.includes: Ritual obligation, significance, synchronization, cost, and the entrenchment of customary practice.
families.exclusions: A single performance treated merely as behavior, physiological synchrony (Biological), or formal ceremonial requirements (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Sacredness, Taboo & Moral Boundaries
families.definition: Shared cultural conditions that mark objects, values, acts, or categories as sacred, prohibited, polluted, or non-negotiable.
families.includes: Culture-level sacred commitment, taboo strength, purity norms, moralization, and trade-off prohibitions.
families.exclusions: An individual's moral conviction (Psychological), legal prohibition (Institutional / Structural), and taboo-violating content (Informational).

families.name: Selfhood, Agency & Relational Models
families.definition: Shared cultural models of what a person is, how agency should be expressed, and how selves should relate to others.
families.includes: Publicly reproduced models of autonomous, relational, or collective personhood and culturally favored ways of exercising agency.
families.exclusions: An individual's self-construal, identity salience, perceived agency, or motivation, which remain Psychological.

families.name: Shared Values & Moral Priorities
families.definition: Culture-level prominence of broadly desirable goals and moral priorities that organize collective judgments and trade-offs.
families.includes: Shared value emphases measured at a specified community, subculture, organization, region, nation, or transnational cultural level.
families.exclusions: Individual value endorsement (Psychological), formal policy priorities (Institutional / Structural), and observed behavior without evidence of shared valuation.

families.name: Acoustic, Visual & Vibrational Conditions
families.definition: Ambient sound, light, visual complexity, and mechanical vibration exposures.
families.includes: Include sound level and pattern, speech masking, illuminance, daylight, spectrum, glare, clutter, and vibration.
families.exclusions: Exclude hearing damage, fatigue, alertness, and perceived annoyance as internal responses.

families.name: Air, Chemical & Environmental Quality
families.definition: Airflow, pollutant, odor, sanitation, dampness, allergen, radiation, smoke, and contamination exposures.
families.includes: Include measurable environmental concentrations and material cleanliness conditions.
families.exclusions: Exclude biomarkers, symptoms, disease, and beliefs about contamination.

families.name: Built Form & Spatial Configuration
families.definition: Physical geometry and arrangement of buildings, rooms, entries, exits, circulation, furniture, and enclosure.
families.includes: Include layout complexity, sightlines, entry/egress geometry, vertical circulation, seating, openness, and structural integrity.
families.exclusions: Exclude authorization rules, social meaning, and subjective safety or preference.

families.name: Density, Confinement & Privacy Conditions
families.definition: Objective occupancy, spacing, flow restriction, enclosure, and acoustic or visual separation conditions.
families.includes: Include occupancy density, interpersonal distance, privacy affordances, queues, bottlenecks, and confinement.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived crowding, relational closeness, preferences, and social monitoring itself.

families.name: Environmental Affordances & Legibility
families.definition: Physically instantiated cues, placements, obstacles, and choice-set features that make actions visible, intelligible, easy, or difficult.
families.includes: Include landmark salience, physical signage placement, option visibility/proximity/availability, and obstacles.
families.exclusions: Exclude message wording, subjective salience, perceived ease, and broad friction catch-alls.

families.name: Hazards, Safety & Physical Security
families.definition: Material hazard intensity, proximity, visibility, refuge, access-control, and evacuation-route conditions.
families.includes: Include hazard distance/intensity, illumination, passive observability, barriers, exits, shelter, flood, fire, and structural hazards.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived threat, warnings, policing, credentials, and formal emergency orders.

families.name: Material Resources & Shelter
families.definition: Physical presence, quantity, location, and usability of food, water, sanitation, shelter, energy, fuel, medical material, and equipment.
families.includes: Include resource availability, point-of-use placement, and housing or shelter condition.
families.exclusions: Exclude affordability, allocation policy, entitlement, subjective scarcity, and digital capability.

families.name: Mobility & Transport Infrastructure
families.definition: Material transport facilities and traffic conditions that alter movement feasibility, safety, delay, and mode choice.
families.includes: Include paths, crossings, cycling facilities, transit-stop access, parking, traffic, congestion, and route redundancy.
families.exclusions: Exclude fares, schedules, service policy, enforcement, and app-based routing.

families.name: Natural Environment & Ecological Exposure
families.definition: Availability, accessibility, quality, and dose of natural settings and ecological features.
families.includes: Include green/blue space, vegetation, natural views, biodiversity, and nature-exposure dose.
families.exclusions: Exclude affinity for nature, restorative feeling, and environmental identity.

families.name: Physical Disruption & Passability
families.definition: Event-driven loss of material system function, passability, access, or environmental continuity.
families.includes: Include specified infrastructure functionality, route blockage, debris, and materially caused access loss.
families.exclusions: Exclude administrative closure, supply-chain governance, displacement as an outcome, and vague instability.

families.name: Spatial Access & Proximity
families.definition: Spatial distance, reach, connectivity, and isolation conditions that determine whether destinations can be reached.
families.includes: Include objective distance, directness, connectivity, density, remoteness, and barrier-free reach.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived distance, relational closeness, formal access rules, and navigation algorithms.

families.name: Terrain, Topography & Geographic Barriers
families.definition: Landform and elevation conditions that alter physical effort, visibility, access, and movement options.
families.includes: Include slope, ruggedness, altitude, water barriers, and chokepoints.
families.exclusions: Exclude map information, border policy, capability limitations, and physiological hypoxia.

families.name: Thermal, Atmospheric & Weather Conditions
families.definition: External thermal and meteorological exposures that alter comfort, effort, performance, and protective behavior.
families.includes: Include heat, cold, humidity, precipitation, wind, solar load, day length, and severe-weather intensity.
families.exclusions: Exclude thermoregulation, heat strain, hypothermia, and risk perception.

families.name: Administrative Burden & Procedural Friction
families.definition: Learning, documentation, procedural, timing, compliance, renewal, and channel requirements created by formal systems.
families.includes: Include required steps, forms, delays, deadlines, recertification, and default enrollment rules.
families.exclusions: Exclude physical distance, subjective effort alone, and information complexity not created by institutional procedure.

families.name: Corruption, Patronage & Institutional Integrity
families.definition: Misuse of formal authority, private-interest capture, patronage, clientelism, bribery opportunity, and integrity safeguards.
families.includes: Include corrupt practice prevalence, patronage allocation, clientelist exchange, procurement transparency, and conflict-of-interest controls.
families.exclusions: Exclude generalized mistrust, informal reciprocity, criminal outcomes, and cultural tolerance of corruption.

families.name: Formal Rules & Authority Allocation
families.definition: Formal permissions, obligations, prohibitions, eligibility boundaries, roles, and allocations of decision authority.
families.includes: Include formal rule content, decision rights, discretion, review rights, and property or control rights.
families.exclusions: Exclude informal cultural norms, individual perceived authority, and immediate interpersonal influence.

families.name: Incentives, Sanctions & Payoffs
families.definition: Institutionally specified rewards, costs, benefits, penalties, liability, and contingency structures.
families.includes: Include tax rates, fees, subsidies, sanctions, reward magnitude, sanction graduation, and liability allocation.
families.exclusions: Exclude intrinsic motivation, market prices absent institutional design, and informal social approval.

families.name: Interorganizational & Multilevel Governance
families.definition: Formal dependencies, overlaps, pressures, and coordination arrangements among organizations and jurisdictions.
families.includes: Include resource dependence, interdependence, jurisdictional overlap, coordination fragmentation, and coercive, mimetic, or professional pressure.
families.exclusions: Exclude social-network ties and information exchange not embedded in formal arrangements.

families.name: Market, Labor & Transaction Structure
families.definition: Formal economic rules governing exchange, entry, competition, contracting, ownership, procurement, and employment.
families.includes: Include transaction costs, competition, concentration, entry barriers, procurement, contract rules, and employment protections.
families.exclusions: Exclude individual prices or preferences and purely technological platforms.

families.name: Monitoring, Enforcement & Accountability
families.definition: Formal monitoring, enforcement, disclosure, performance-control, oversight, surveillance-mandate, and consequence systems.
families.includes: Include audit intensity, sanction certainty, reporting, transparency rules, performance regimes, feedback, oversight, and accountability consequences.
families.exclusions: Exclude technological sensor capability, peer observation, perceived surveillance, and reputational sanctions.

families.name: Organizational Structure & Work Design
families.definition: Formal organizational configuration, division of labor, hierarchy, formalization, workload, and coordination design.
families.includes: Include centralization, formalization, standardization, specialization, hierarchy, span, departments, role clarity, mandate conflict, and caseload.
families.exclusions: Exclude informal culture, friendship networks, personality, and physical workspace design.

families.name: Participation, Procedural Governance & Redress
families.definition: Formal voice, representation, inclusion, impartial procedure, explanation, appeals, grievance, and self-governance arrangements.
families.includes: Include collective-choice participation, representation, procedural consistency, reason-giving, redress, and local autonomy.
families.exclusions: Exclude felt fairness, cultural democratic values, and informal conflict mediation.

families.name: Policy Stability & Institutional Change
families.definition: Temporal durability, review, emergency authority, switching cost, precedent, and learning properties of formal systems.
families.includes: Include policy stability, switching costs, emergency powers, sunset clauses, precedent strength, and organizational learning capacity.
families.exclusions: Exclude path dependence and policy feedback when used only as explanatory frameworks or mechanisms.

families.name: Political Power, Rights & Differential Treatment
families.definition: Formal and de facto allocations of political power, legal status, rights, exclusion, segregation, and unequal application.
families.includes: Include political power, discrimination, differential enforcement, segregation, rights deprivation, veto points, censorship, and border controls.
families.exclusions: Exclude personal prejudice, cultural hierarchy norms, and physical separation without institutional production.

families.name: Resource Distribution, Eligibility & Service Access
families.definition: Formal allocation, rationing, priority, jurisdictional coverage, gatekeeping, and distributional arrangements.
families.includes: Include budget allocation, structural service coverage, quotas, queue rules, geographic allocation, gatekeeping, and distributional inequality.
families.exclusions: Exclude material stocks and distance, subjective scarcity, and interpersonal resource sharing.

families.name: State Capacity & Legal-Institutional Quality
families.definition: Institutional ability to raise resources, staff functions, administer territory, enforce law, deliver services, and sustain impartial legal order.
families.includes: Include fiscal, personnel, administrative, analytic, territorial, judicial, and regulatory capacities.
families.exclusions: Exclude physical infrastructure stock, perceived legitimacy or trust, and broad country labels.

families.name: Action Guidance & Instructional Content
families.definition: Message features that specify a recommended action, implementation steps, timing, and decision-relevant constraints.
families.includes: Include recommendation specificity, calls to action, step completeness, and deadline specificity.
families.exclusions: Exclude behavior itself, opportunity, enforcement, and interface affordances.

families.name: Argument & Evidence Quality
families.definition: Strength, amount, type, traceability, and explanatory structure of reasons and evidence supporting a claim.
families.includes: Include logical strength, evidence quality and amount, quantitative or exemplar evidence, citations, and causal explanation.
families.exclusions: Exclude recipient elaboration and institutional evidence rules.

families.name: Clarity, Complexity & Completeness
families.definition: Linguistic and structural properties governing how explicit, readable, ambiguous, conflicting, or complete a message is.
families.includes: Include readability, complexity, ambiguity, completeness, contradiction, and uncertainty expression.
families.exclusions: Exclude comprehension, confusion, numeracy, and perceived uncertainty.

families.name: Feedback, Comparison & Norm Claims
families.definition: Communicated information about performance, progress, benchmarks, prevalence, approval, or consensus.
families.includes: Include performance feedback, comparative benchmarks, descriptive-norm claims, and consensus claims.
families.exclusions: Exclude actual norms, social approval, rank, and feedback-delivery technology.

families.name: Framing & Presentation
families.definition: How substantively similar content is worded, ordered, formatted, or visually represented.
families.includes: Include gain/loss and attribute frames, probability formats, metaphors, ordering, and graphics.
families.exclusions: Exclude interface ranking and any claim that one frame is universally superior.

families.name: Information Availability & Exposure
families.definition: Whether behavior-relevant information is present, discoverable, noticeable, current, and encountered for sufficient time at a decision point.
families.includes: Include message availability, salience, recency, cues, and exposure duration.
families.exclusions: Exclude platform access and ranking, physical placement, and the recipient’s attention state.

families.name: Information Volume, Density & Load
families.definition: Objective amount, rate, density, and length of information presented within a defined exposure window.
families.includes: Include item count, arrival rate, message length, and content density.
families.exclusions: Exclude subjective overload and cognitive capacity, which are Psychological.
representativeDrivers: Information Volume Relative to Exposure Window

families.name: Narrative, Exemplification & Vividness
families.definition: Message features that organize information as stories, cases, concrete imagery, emotional content, or warnings.
families.includes: Include narrative form and coherence, exemplars, vividness, emotional valence/intensity, and warning content.
families.exclusions: Exclude narrative transportation, emotion experienced, and culturally shared master narratives.

families.name: Relevance, Tailoring & Audience Match
families.definition: Message adaptations that align content with a specified person, location, language, culture, or audience context.
families.includes: Include personalization, local specificity, linguistic accessibility, and cultural-context match.
families.exclusions: Exclude felt self-relevance, identity, and automated targeting systems.

families.name: Repetition, Timing & Sequence
families.definition: Frequency, spacing, timing, ordering, and cross-source convergence of exposures.
families.includes: Include repetition, spacing, correction delay, sequence, and convergence across identifiable sources.
families.exclusions: Exclude algorithmic amplification and memory or familiarity states.

families.name: Risk, Threat & Efficacy Content
families.definition: Stated information about severity, likelihood, susceptibility, response efficacy, and uncertainty of consequential outcomes.
families.includes: Include communicated threat, vulnerability, efficacy, and risk magnitude.
families.exclusions: Exclude fear, perceived threat, perceived vulnerability, and efficacy beliefs.

families.name: Source Disclosure & Provenance
families.definition: Information conveyed about who produced a claim, their relevant qualifications and interests, and the claim’s origin and processing history.
families.includes: Include identity, credentials, track record, motive, conflicts, provenance, process transparency, and consensus cues.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived credibility or trust and actual interpersonal relationships.

families.name: Veracity, Omission & Correction
families.definition: Accuracy, misleadingness, omission, correction, retraction, and explanatory content that updates a claim.
families.includes: Include factual veracity, omission magnitude, correction presence/detail/specificity, and alternative explanations.
families.exclusions: Exclude belief accuracy and deliberate intent unless separately evidenced.

families.name: Access, Infrastructure & Interoperability
families.definition: Technical capabilities that determine whether a digital function is available, reachable, compatible, mobile, accessible, and usable under varying connectivity conditions.
families.includes: Include devices, network capacity, uptime, functional reliability, compatibility, interoperability, offline operation, and assistive-technology support.
families.exclusions: Exclude affordability and distribution rules, physical distance, and user skill.

families.name: Algorithmic Curation & Adaptive Delivery
families.definition: Computational selection, ranking, amplification, filtering, personalization, and context-responsive delivery of options or information.
families.includes: Include measurable allocation weights, filters, personalization intensity, and update sensitivity.
families.exclusions: Exclude message meaning, user preference, and causal feedback-loop narratives without a specified system parameter.

families.name: Attention, Interruption & Temporal Control
families.definition: System features governing alerts, prompts, interruption intensity, delivery timing, automatic continuation, feed endpoints, and stopping cues.
families.includes: Include technological cue delivery and temporal interaction structure.
families.exclusions: Exclude prompt wording, attention state, habit, and campaign policy.

families.name: Automation Reliability & Decision Support
families.definition: System performance and automation properties that determine what decision work is automated and how reliable recommendations and alarms are.
families.includes: Include automation level, decision-aid reliability, recommendation availability, and alarm error rates.
families.exclusions: Exclude human trust, automation bias, and institutional authority to deploy the system.

families.name: Digital Feedback, Rewards & Gamification
families.definition: Digitally implemented reactions, status metrics, rankings, rewards, streaks, schedules, and progress displays.
families.includes: Include technical feedback and reinforcement structures.
families.exclusions: Exclude social approval, intrinsic motivation, subjective progress, and reward policy outside the system.

families.name: Human–AI Social Interaction
families.definition: AI interface properties that instantiate humanlike cues, reciprocal dialogue, persistent relational memory, affective response, and identity continuity.
families.includes: Include AI-specific interaction capabilities that can elicit social responses.
families.exclusions: Exclude the user’s anthropomorphism, trust, attachment, or felt social presence.

families.name: Human Control, Explainability & AI Collaboration
families.definition: Technical controls and interaction features supporting uncertainty display, explanation, verification, override, approval, and collaborative division of work.
families.includes: Include machine-confidence displays, explanation interfaces, verifiability tools, override controls, approval gates, and interaction-pattern flexibility.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived control, trust, comprehension, and legal accountability.

families.name: Immersion, Embodiment & Representation
families.definition: Technical properties governing sensory envelopment, avatar control, sensorimotor coupling, modality breadth, fidelity, realism, and remote interaction synchrony.
families.includes: Include mediated representation and immersive-system capabilities.
families.exclusions: Exclude felt presence, body ownership, identity meaning, and cultural stereotypes.

families.name: Interface Choice Architecture
families.definition: Interface configurations that alter defaults, ordering, friction, prominence, simplification, active choice, and disclosure encounter.
families.includes: Include measurable UI states and interaction pathways that shape feasible selections.
families.exclusions: Exclude semantic content, recipient perception, and broad labels such as dark patterns when no atomic feature is specified.

families.name: Platform Social Affordances
families.definition: Platform action possibilities for visibility, persistence, search, replication, reach, association, identity disclosure, and editing.
families.includes: Include technical affordances that enable social action and information movement.
families.exclusions: Exclude the resulting network structure, norms, identity meaning, and content itself.

families.name: Privacy, Security & Identity Architecture
families.definition: Technical configurations controlling data collection, privacy choice, authentication burden, identity verification, access restriction, and retention.
families.includes: Include system-enforced privacy, authentication, authorization, and retention parameters.
families.exclusions: Exclude privacy concern, organizational policy, legal requirements, and threat intent.

families.name: Sensing, Monitoring & Traceability
families.definition: Technical capability to sense, log, display, observe, and reconstruct behavior or system events.
families.includes: Include self-monitoring, automated feedback, tracking visibility, third-party observability, and event logs.
families.exclusions: Exclude surveillance authority, sanctions, and perceived surveillance.

families.name: Synthetic Media & Agentic Capabilities
families.definition: Technical capabilities for autonomous action, external tool use, synthetic-content generation, scalable production, representational fidelity, and provenance signaling.
families.includes: Include measurable autonomy and generative-system capabilities.
families.exclusions: Exclude the veracity or meaning of generated content, user belief, and institutional authorization.
